newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - Malawi - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Malawi - April 30.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Wednesday April 30.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Riot police on Tuesday used teargas to disperse marching government primary school teachers in Blantyre, Lilongwe and Mzuzu who were protesting against poor salaries. Meanwhile police are still holding in custody Civil Servants Trade Union vice president Thomas Mwafongo.

- The directive by Justice Minister Cassim Chilumpha, who ordered that no jury should be used to try former President Kamuzu Banda in a K137-million fraud case is suspicious, defending lawyer Bernard O'Sullivan said in court on Tuesday.

- Police in all of Malawi's three regions -- acting on orders from the Inspector General to deal with anyone defying their orders -- on Tuesday stepped up brutality against striking civil servants by beating and arresting their leaders.

- An industrial specialist lawyer, Viva Nyimba, said on Tuesday it was unfortunate that Justice Minister Cassim Chilumpha slammed the door on further negotiations with striking civil servants when he told a local newspaper that there was no room for talks with public workers.
